chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Boston neighborhoods and boyhood schoolmates Carney, Hodges and Howard Johnson
summary: He corrects the interviewer on streets lived on (Warwick, Marble, Roxbury) and recalls meeting Johnny Hodges, Harry Carney and Howard Johnson around Sherwin Grammar School.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, you lived on Tremont Street?
Holmes (10/9) - 2

No. Never lived on Tremont Street in my life. My family lived in... Well, in Boston we lived on Warwick Street. Then we moved to Marble Street. And after Marble Street, we moved out in Roxbury to Harrishaw(?) Street.

Now, while I was on Warwick Street, that's when I was going to grammar school, the Sherwin Grammar School. Around about that time... This was, oh, let me see, in the years... Quite a few years back there. Anyway, that's when I met Howard Johnson, Johnny Hodges, Harry Carney. Harry and I were in the same class in school
Now, Harry is supposed to have lived on Cunard Street.
Can-ard Street.
That's right. And Johnny Hodges lived on Cambridge Street, and then he moved to Hammond Street.
Well, I knew him when he lived on Hammond Street. I don't know if there is a Cambridge Street. He lived in Cambridge.
Oh, he lived in Cambridge. That's right. You're right. He lived in Cambridge, and moved to Hammond Street. Then, just around the corner from Hodges, on Shumond(?) Avenue...
Shawmet(?) Avenue, it should be.
On Shawmet(?) Avenue was Howard Johnson.
Holmes (10/9) - 3
That's right. He's from a big musical family, too.
Was Howard in any of your classes, too?
No. Howard was ahead of me at school. There was two years difference in our ages. Naturally, age will make you... A two years difference, you know.
And Hodges was ahead of you, too.

No, Hodges was... He's three years older than I was. But see, by changing from school to school, he was a little bit behind, I think. I don't know... He might have been ahead of me in school. But I don't remember him being in school too long, because he was in Cambridge most of the time. He lived in Cambridge. Just before he started coming to New York, he moved to Boston -- Hammond Street. He lived on Hammond Street quite a while, but I mean, he was...
That's when you knew him, though.
Yeah. He was traveling back and forth.
And that was your neighborhood.
Yeah.
Where was that in terms of Boston? South Side?
No, that was in what they call... Well, that was called Roxbury. That was Roxbury.
Have you been back to the neighborhood at all?
Holmes (10/9) - 4

Well, I went back quite a few times after I came to New York, when my family was living. When my mother and father were alive, I'd go back to visit them and the family, and I'd go around to all the neighborhoods, one thing or another... Yeah. I went back quite a few times.
The neighborhood has changed a lot, or has it stayed the same?

Well, now I wouldn't know. Because the school burned down. I don't know if it was ever rebuilt or not. As all neighborhoods change, I imagine they had their changes, too. Of course, we're going back about sixty-some years now.
